title: Implement Graceful Shutdown for Spring Boot Application
question: Your Spring Boot microservice handles long-running requests (up to 30 seconds). When deploying new versions, in-flight requests are abruptly terminated, causing errors for users. Implement graceful shutdown that: 1) Stops accepting new requests immediately, 2) Waits for in-flight requests to complete (with 60-second timeout), 3) Closes database connections and releases resources properly, 4) Updates health check to 'unhealthy' so load balancer stops routing traffic, 5) Logs shutdown progress. Use Spring Boot shutdown properties, actuator endpoints, and @PreDestroy hooks. Discuss: handling requests exceeding timeout, integration with Kubernetes termination lifecycle, and database connection pool draining.
realWorldScenario: Zero-downtime deployments with proper resource cleanup

title: Optimize Spring Boot Application Startup Time
question: Your Spring Boot application takes 45 seconds to start, causing issues with Kubernetes readiness probes (30-second timeout) and slow deployment cycles. The application has 200+ beans, multiple database connections, and external service dependencies. Optimize startup to under 20 seconds by: 1) Using lazy initialization strategically, 2) Optimizing component scanning, 3) Parallel bean initialization, 4) Avoiding heavy operations in @PostConstruct, 5) Using GraalVM native image or Spring Boot 3 AOT. Measure with startup actuator endpoint. Discuss: trade-offs of lazy initialization, identifying slow beans, warm-up strategies, and impact on first request latency.
realWorldScenario: Optimizing application startup for cloud deployments

title: Implement Dynamic Configuration Refresh Without Restart
question: Your application needs to update configuration (feature flags, rate limits, external URLs) without restart. Configuration is stored in Spring Cloud Config Server / Consul. Implement dynamic refresh that: 1) Detects configuration changes from config server, 2) Refreshes @ConfigurationProperties beans, 3) Notifies affected components to reload, 4) Supports manual refresh via /actuator/refresh endpoint, 5) Handles refresh failures gracefully (keep old config). Use @RefreshScope, Spring Cloud Config, and configuration change events. Discuss: which beans can be refreshed vs need restart, avoiding mid-request configuration changes, thread safety during refresh, and validation of new configuration.

title: Build Real-Time Metrics Dashboard Using Actuator and Micrometer
question: Build a real-time monitoring dashboard for your Spring Boot application showing: 1) Request rate, latency percentiles (p50, p95, p99), 2) JVM memory and GC metrics, 3) Database connection pool stats, 4) Custom business metrics (orders/minute, failed payments), 5) Alert when error rate exceeds threshold. Use Spring Boot Actuator, Micrometer, Prometheus, and Grafana. Implement custom metrics with Tags for filtering (by endpoint, status code, user type). Discuss: metric naming conventions, cardinality explosion risks (avoid high-cardinality tags like user_id), histogram vs summary for latency, and metric retention strategies.
realWorldScenario: Production monitoring with metrics and alerting

title: Implement Distributed Tracing Across Microservices
question: Your system has 15 microservices. A single user request flows through 5-6 services. When performance issues occur, it's hard to identify which service is slow. Implement distributed tracing using Spring Cloud Sleuth and Zipkin/Jaeger that: 1) Automatically propagates trace and span IDs across services, 2) Traces HTTP calls (RestTemplate, WebClient, Feign), 3) Traces async operations (@Async, message queues), 4) Traces database queries, 5) Adds custom spans for business operations. Visualize traces in Zipkin UI. Discuss: sampling strategy (trace 100% in dev, 10% in prod), performance overhead, trace context propagation across threads, and correlation with logs (MDC).

title: Design Bulk Data Processing with Batch Jobs
question: Build a nightly batch job that processes 10 million records from database, applies business rules, and exports results to S3. Requirements: 1) Process in chunks to avoid memory issues, 2) Skip failed records, continue processing, 3) Track progress (completed/failed counts), 4) Support restart from last checkpoint if interrupted, 5) Parallel processing for speed. Use Spring Batch with chunk-oriented processing, ItemReader/ItemWriter, and job repository. Discuss: chunk size optimization, transaction boundaries, error handling strategies (skip vs retry vs fail), parallel step execution, and monitoring batch job metrics via actuator.

title: Implement API Versioning Strategy for REST APIs
question: Your public REST API has 10,000+ external clients. You need to release backward-incompatible changes. Design API versioning that supports: 1) Multiple versions concurrently (v1, v2), 2) Version specified in URL (/api/v1/users) or header (X-API-Version), 3) Shared business logic between versions (avoid code duplication), 4) Gradual client migration with deprecation warnings, 5) Sunset old versions after 6 months. Use @RequestMapping with version paths, custom RequestCondition, or content negotiation. Discuss: versioning strategy (URI vs header vs accept header), maintaining multiple versions, deprecation policy communication, and version-specific documentation.

title: Secure External Configuration with HashiCorp Vault
question: Your application needs to access secrets (database passwords, API keys, encryption keys) securely. Storing them in application.properties is insecure. Integrate HashiCorp Vault for secret management: 1) Fetch secrets from Vault at startup, 2) Inject secrets as @Value or @ConfigurationProperties, 3) Rotate secrets without restart (refresh secrets periodically), 4) Use dynamic database credentials (Vault generates temp credentials), 5) Audit all secret access. Use Spring Cloud Vault. Discuss: authentication with Vault (token, AppRole, Kubernetes), secret renewal before expiry, handling Vault unavailability at startup, and fallback to cached secrets.

title: Implement Schema-Based Multi-Tenancy with Dynamic DataSource
question: Build a multi-tenant SaaS application where each tenant has their own database schema (tenant1, tenant2). A single Spring Boot instance serves all tenants. Implement: 1) Identify tenant from subdomain/header, 2) Route database queries to correct schema using Spring's AbstractRoutingDataSource, 3) Ensure transaction isolation (no cross-tenant data leakage), 4) Support adding new tenants without restart, 5) Connection pooling per tenant. Use Hibernate multi-tenancy, schema resolver, and thread-local tenant context. Discuss: tenant context propagation to async tasks, schema migration for all tenants (Flyway/Liquibase), connection pool sizing, and handling tenant onboarding.

title: Implement Resilience Patterns with Resilience4j
question: Your microservice calls external payment gateway API that sometimes fails or is slow. Implement resilience patterns using Resilience4j: 1) Circuit Breaker (stop calling if too many failures), 2) Retry with exponential backoff, 3) Rate Limiter (max 100 calls/second to API), 4) Bulkhead (isolate thread pool for external calls), 5) Timeout (fail fast if call takes >5 seconds). Use Resilience4j annotations (@CircuitBreaker, @Retry, @RateLimiter) and Spring Boot integration. Expose circuit breaker state via actuator. Discuss: circuit breaker state transitions (closed/open/half-open), configuring failure thresholds, fallback methods, and combining patterns (retry with circuit breaker).
